comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C45-C48 regarding CMK-1's genetic role in adaptation. Both evaluations find the loss-of-function and gain-of-function data compelling and well-supported, with reviewers noting strong effect sizes.

Perfect agreement on claims C49-C52 regarding calcineurin's requirement for adaptation. Both evaluations accept the pharmacological and genetic evidence, with reviewers praising the elegant use of loss and gain-of-function approaches.

Perfect agreement on claims C61-C68 regarding CMK-1's cell-specific localization to AFD/ASER. Both evaluations find the cell-specific rescue and ablation experiments convincing, with reviewers highlighting the strength of the genetic model system for cellular mapping.

Strong agreement on claims C53-C60 regarding complex genetic interactions between CMK-1 and calcineurin. Both evaluations accept the epistasis data and non-linear pathway model. Peer review includes C88 which OpenEval addresses separately in R11.

Strong agreement on claims C69-C74 regarding TAX-6's cell-specific localization to FLP and interneurons (especially RIM). Both evaluations accept the cell-specific overexpression data. Peer review also includes C95-C96 which OpenEval addresses separately in R13.

Partial overlap on phosphoproteomics screen validation (C3, C39-C42). Both evaluations support the screen methodology. OpenEval R1 also covers in vitro kinase assays (C4, C43-C44) while peer R1 emphasizes dataset limitations (C75, C79, C80, C82) that OpenEval addresses in R8.

Partial overlap on in vitro phosphorylation evidence (C4, C43-C44). Both evaluations find the biochemical data compelling. OpenEval R1 covers broader kinase assay evidence while peer R2 focuses specifically on the conserved site and includes C84 (prior work context).

Critical disagreement on claims C9, C85 regarding physiological relevance of direct phosphorylation. OpenEval finds the circuit-level antagonism interpretation well-supported and logical. Peer reviewers explicitly identify this as UNCERTAIN, noting a disconnect between in vitro phosphorylation and in vivo behavioral relevance due to different cellular localizations.

Partial overlap on phosphoproteomics limitations (C75, C79, C80, C82). Both evaluations accept the authors' acknowledgment of dataset limitations as appropriate scientific caution. OpenEval R8 covers broader methodological concerns (C76-C78) while peer R1 focuses on screen validation.

Partial overlap on dataset limitations (C76-C78). Both evaluations accept these as reasonable caveats about in vitro screening approaches. OpenEval R8 includes additional claims about GO enrichment and low overlap between methods.

Partial overlap on circuit-level interpretation (C10-C11). OpenEval finds the antagonistic circuit model well-supported. Peer reviewers accept the model that CMK-1 and calcineurin act in separate neurons antagonistically, also including claims C5-C6 about the overall findings.

Partial overlap on cell-specific effects (C95-C96). Both evaluations accept the differential effects of calcineurin depending on neuron type and experience. OpenEval R13 also includes C97 about experience-dependent effects.
Minimal overlap on prior work context (C84). Both evaluations accept the citation of previous studies showing conserved phosphorylation sites. OpenEval R9 also includes C83 about other kinases.

Minimal overlap on claim C88 regarding rescue of adaptation by joint inhibition. Both evaluations find this key observation well-supported by the data in Figure 3A, supporting the regulatory rather than executive role of these pathways.

OpenEval R10 addresses background knowledge claims C86-C87 about protein expression and activation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these are treated as established field knowledge providing context.

OpenEval R12 addresses prior work claims C89-C94 about FLP and AFD neuron properties. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these citations provide essential background for interpreting current results.
OpenEval R14 addresses background claims C98-C99 about interneuron roles in reversal behavior. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these are established facts cited for context.

OpenEval R15 addresses claim C100 about TAX-6 acting as a dominant gate in interneurons. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; this inference is based on epistasis and cell-specific expression data.

OpenEval R16 addresses extensive background claims C1-C2, C12-C38 establishing study rationale and model system relevance. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these are properly cited prior knowledge contextualizing the study.

Peer R9 addresses overall findings and model (C5-C6, C10-C11) with explicit editor and reviewer endorsement of the antagonistic circuit model. OpenEval addresses these claims partially in R7 and R16, but peer review provides unique explicit validation of the study's value and main conclusions.
